institution_matches.title: Feedback Completion Certificates for Repeated Dwell Tasks with Time Windows
institution_matches.overview: The paper analyzes repeated dwell tasks with time windows under bounded disturbances and shows that, for a common spatial predicate and dwell length with redundant windows removed, the remaining obligations can be ordered so that on any valid history the served windows form a suffix, implying that one boundary and one capped run length suffice as a feedback completion certificate for future satisfaction. Using this reduced state, the authors construct feedback policies over a verified library of branching motion primitives, proving that for one task type a scalar threshold per run length suffices and can be computed with work linear in the number of branches per time layer for fixed dwell, while multiple task types require a joint recursion. In simulations on a quadrotor inspection library and a two-station MuJoCo patrol, threshold-based completion filters reduce the cost of constructing reusable full-domain policies and, compared to a sparse Boolean baseline and safety-only filters, more reliably retain task completion certificates—preserving them in all 8 of 8 initially certified runs versus 3 of 8 for safety-only filtering—while still meeting all time windows in the tested runs.

institution_matches.title: RoboLiveMem: Is Robot Memory Solved When the World Does Not Wait?
institution_matches.institution: Carnegie Mellon University; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; UC San Diego
institution_matches.overview: The paper introduces RoboLiveMem, a benchmark that evaluates robot memory when the world continues to change during decision-making by running identical tasks twice—once with the simulator paused while the model thinks and once with the world running—across 29 task families spanning realistic BEHAVIOR-1K home/workshop/restaurant scenes and controlled ManiSkill tasks. On 34,176 episodes with 16 models, RoboLiveMem reveals that paused evaluations mask severe degradation under live changes: in realistic scenes where a remembered object changes, eight Claude and GPT models average 97% success with the world paused but only 50% with it running, with some models (e.g., Claude Opus 5.5) dropping from never failing when paused to 44% success when live. Analysis shows that lower inference latency does not solve the problem—models with only 2 s per decision still lose at least 36 percentage points relative to paused performance—and that models often perceive changes but act on stale frames; adding a final look before acting closes much of this gap in realistic settings, yet under repeated identical-object swaps all nine tested models still lose performance due to memory limitations.

institution_matches.title: One Policy, Many Bodies: Cooperative Human-Object Interaction with Heterogeneous Teams
institution_matches.overview: The paper presents MorphHOI, a decentralized physics-based human-object interaction framework that enables cooperative manipulation across heterogeneous embodiments by introducing a canonical body interface to unify observation and action spaces and an embodiment-conditioned transformer that tailors cooperative decisions to each agent’s physical capabilities and team composition. MorphHOI extends to new interaction skills by reusing the learned cooperative policy with task-specific tokens and lightweight adaptation, aiming to add new capabilities while preserving previously learned cooperation behaviors. In simulation, MorphHOI achieves cooperative transport success rates up to 96.7% on seen embodiments, 95.6% on unseen embodiments, and 91.4% on novel payloads, and maintains high success across diverse skills such as box carrying, stair transport, and waypoint following while preserving prior cooperative capabilities.

institution_matches.title: DUO Policy: Bridging Human Video Coverage and Robot Precision for Fine-Grained Manipulation
institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes DUO Policy, a dual-actor manipulation framework that splits control into a hand policy pretrained on human videos for global free-space motion and a robot policy trained on sparse in-hand data for local precise corrections, with a learned gate (trained from human interventions) switching between them based on state-dependent precision requirements. By leveraging human data primarily where precision demands are low and robot data near precision-critical states, DUO Policy is designed to tolerate moderate embodiment mismatch in human videos while generalizing to scene layouts beyond those covered by robot data alone. On fine-grained manipulation tasks such as K-cup coffee making, desk cleanup, and cluttered candy sorting, DUO Policy outperforms the strongest baseline by an average of 12.9 percentage points across four simulated tasks and 51.7 points across three real-world tasks, and matches the performance of robot-only training with 2.75× less robot data collection time.

institution_matches.title: JEPA-ICL: Progress-Aligned Latent Plans for In-Context Robotic Manipulation
institution_matches.overview: The paper introduces JEPA-ICL, a vision-language-action framework that learns predictive plans in JEPA feature space by forecasting ordered future states up to subtask completion, thereby encoding what remains to be done and using these latent plans both to guide action generation and to align demonstrations with the robot’s current progress. JEPA-ICL leverages JEPA-supervised content features to locate progress-matched segments in demonstrations and uses this contextual guidance during training and inference to update a shared policy that jointly produces plans and actions, coupling self-prediction with demonstration reuse. On the Imitator Game benchmark, JEPA-ICL reaches 80.0% success on seen tasks under C15 pretraining, outperforming Zero-WAM by 12.0 percentage points; without contextual demonstrations it improves success from 96.1% to 97.6% on LIBERO and from 62.9% to 73.2% on LIBERO-Plus compared to a VLA-JEPA variant without human-video pretraining, and with demonstration-based training plus contextual guidance further boosts LIBERO-Plus success from 73.2% to 75.2%.

topic_matches.title: Neural Fidelity Calibration: Turning Field Anomalies into Simulation Fine-Tuning
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes Neural Fidelity Calibration (NFC), a conditional flow matching–based framework that infers, online and from robot execution data, posterior distributions over both simulator physical parameters and residual fidelity terms capturing unmodeled dynamics and discrepancies between perceived and true environment geometry. NFC uses a simulation-trained anomaly detector on onboard sensory signals to decide when to trigger recalibration or fine-tuning and employs an exploration policy that modulates posterior uncertainty via optimism in the face of uncertainty to improve inference quality. Across five robot platforms with up to 39 calibrated parameters and a 128×128 residual terrain map, NFC yields more accurate posterior estimates than established simulation-based inference baselines and, in physical outdoor tests with a wheeled robot with an axle failure on snow, mud, and wet grass, increases rough-terrain navigation success from 26% to 70% while reducing orientation jerk by 88%.

topic_matches.title: Neural Fidelity Calibration for Informative Sim-to-Real Adaptation
topic_matches.institution: Luddy School of Informatics, Computing, and Engineering Indiana University
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes Neural Fidelity Calibration (NFC), which uses conditional flow matching to jointly calibrate simulator physical parameters and a high-dimensional residual fidelity domain online during deployment, capturing both sim-to-real dynamics discrepancies and perception-induced environment uncertainty in a latent space for posterior sampling and policy fine-tuning. NFC includes an informative adaptation scheme—fine-tuning is triggered only on anomaly detection, with sequential NFC seeding from a simulation-pretrained estimator and a hallucination policy modulating posterior uncertainty using optimism in the face of uncertainty. Across five robots with up to 39 physical parameters and a 128×128 residual terrain, NFC attains more accurate posteriors than established simulation-based inference methods, and on a wheeled robot with a broken axle on snow, mud, and wet grass, it increases rough-terrain success from 26% to 70% and reduces orientation jerk by 88% in real-world deployment.

topic_matches.title: A Hybrid Multi-Goal Path Planning Framework for Powered Wheelchairs in Dynamic Environments: From Simulation to Real-World Validation
topic_matches.overview: The study presents a hybrid multi-goal path planning framework for autonomous powered wheelchairs that combines TSP-based global task ordering with Potential-Field guidance and local RRT or A* planners, where PF guidance transfers global path information to help the robot stay aligned while avoiding static and dynamic obstacles. Local planning is enhanced using direction-aware, extended-neighborhood A* or RRT with environment-aware sampling and two-step extension, and an elliptical robot model is introduced to explicitly account for wheelchair dimensions during collision avoidance. Simulation evaluations in normal, crowded, and extra-crowded environments, along with hardware tests using motion capture and onboard LiDAR/RGB-D sensing, show that incorporating wheelchair geometry via the elliptical model changes observed collision behavior and yields comparable collision avoidance performance between the TSP-PF-RRT and TSP-PF-A* hybrid planners.

topic_matches.title: Belief-Driven Quantum Magnetometer Control for GPS-Denied Navigation
topic_matches.overview: The paper introduces a belief-driven control rule for Ramsey-type quantum magnetometers in magnetic anomaly navigation, where the navigation filter’s position belief, propagated through the anomaly map, determines the sensor’s phase and interrogation time at each epoch to balance ambiguity and decoherence limits. Evaluated on real U.S. Air Force flight data with only the Ramsey sensor modeled, belief-driven sensing is favored in 63 of 72 independent flight windows over fixed-setting baselines (p = 2×10⁻¹¹), reducing navigation error by 20–27% for low-SNR sensors and 30–44% for mid-contrast sensors, with smaller gains for high-quality sensors with accurate maps. Ablation studies show phase alignment primarily improves steady-flight performance and can match the best hindsight-tuned fixed setting, while interrogation time adaptation is crucial after a lost start, cutting median error by 37–42% even versus hindsight-tuned phase-aligned baselines; on an IBM superconducting qubit, the rule’s interrogation times stay within 1.3× of the empirical optimum, and when combined with information-aware routing, belief-driven sensing reduces mission error by 15–40%.

topic_matches.title: Distilling Touch into Vision-Only Policies for Contact-Rich Manipulation
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes TacitTouch, a distillation framework that trains a vision-only student policy to imitate a frozen visuotactile teacher’s tactile-guided behavior by supervising the student’s denoising predictions and intermediate action representations at matched noisy actions and flow times, supplemented with demonstrated-action supervision, without reconstructing tactile observations. During deployment, TacitTouch uses only visual input and no tactile encoder, expert, or generator, effectively shifting from learning predicted tactile signals to directly learning tactile-guided action patterns. Across four simulated UniVTAC tasks and four real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks, TacitTouch improves mean success rates by 16.0 and 22.5 percentage points over vision-only baselines, while remaining within 2.0 and 3.75 percentage points of the visuotactile teacher, and in robustness tests it outperforms TacImag by up to 20.0 percentage points in mean success rate.

topic_matches.title: VTLA-RL: Learning Visuotactile Policies for Load-Adaptive Grasping
topic_matches.institution: NVIDIA; The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
topic_matches.overview: The paper introduces VTLA-RL, a visuotactile grasping framework that shares a visual encoder between tactile-image histories and RGB inputs to jointly generate and execute motion and bilateral force targets in a unified action space, aiming to handle load-adaptive grasping under varying object masses and slip conditions. VTLA-RL is initialized with mixed real and simulated demonstrations to establish motion and contact priors, and then optimized using two-stage multi-task reinforcement learning solely in simulation, with the resulting policy deployed directly to real robots without further real-data supervision. Comparative evaluations of tactile representations and RL post-training variants in simulation, and hardware tests under load variation and placement perturbations, show that the full VTLA-RL method achieves higher grasping success than its supervised-only initialization and that RL post-training benefits depend on the chosen representation and training route.

topic_matches.title: Spatially Grounded Latent Lookahead for Vision-Language-Action Models
topic_matches.institution: PrismaX Robotics; Shanghai Jiao Tong University
topic_matches.overview: The paper presents Spatially Grounded Latent Lookahead (SG-LL), which augments vision-language-action models by predicting an actionable near-future representation that is spatially grounded in the current scene, using a frozen spatial teacher to distill geometric priors into spatial tokens and a current-conditioned bottleneck to learn a compact future latent without access to future observations. SG-LL predicts the future latent from the current policy context and initial Action Expert features, and fuses this latent into the Action Expert via zero-initialized residual connections to refine action generation while preserving stability at initialization. Experiments on the LIBERO-Plus and CALVIN benchmarks and on three real-world manipulation tasks show that SG-LL improves performance over compared baselines in both simulation and real-robot settings, indicating benefits from spatially grounded lookahead for manipulation.

topic_matches.title: FunGrasp-Zero: Field-Conditioned Graph Attention Policy for Zero-Shot Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Functional Grasping
topic_matches.institution: Shenzhen Loop Area Institute; Sun Yat-sen University; X SQUARE ROBOT
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes FunGrasp-Zero, a reinforcement learning framework for zero-shot cross-embodiment dexterous functional grasping that represents functional intent through an object-centric, embodiment-consistent contact map, which is mapped to diverse hand morphologies and converted into a hand-object potential field providing attractive and repulsive guidance vectors. A Field-Conditioned Graph Attention Network (FC-GAT) conditions multi-finger motion on these potential-field-derived vectors, while a potential field reward encourages fingers to approach target functional regions and penalizes non-target collisions to enforce both functional alignment and grasp stability. On the proposed X-FunBench benchmark, a single policy co-trained on four embodiments achieves an 86% average grasp success rate across five unseen simulated hands on novel objects and, when deployed without fine-tuning on four unseen physical hands (Leap, Inspire, Sharpa, Wuji), attains an 80% average success rate for novel object grasping in real-world experiments.

topic_matches.title: $ζ_0$: A Framework for World Action Models with Joint Scene and Body Foresight in Humanoid Control
topic_matches.institution: Fudan University; Lenovo Group Limited; Shanghai Innovation Institute; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Shanghai University; Tongji University; University of Science and Technology of China; Zhejiang University
topic_matches.overview: The paper introduces ζ₀, a framework that converts vision-language-action policies into World Action Models by jointly predicting future visual features and measured joint trajectories in a shared latent space, using a teacher conditioned on recorded futures and dual-response transfer to train a causal predictor to match both teacher responses and executing-policy actions. ζ₀ trains all components jointly but uses only causally predicted futures at deployment, providing joint scene and body foresight rather than purely visual foresight or unsupervised latent-distance objectives. On seven HumanoidArena tasks, ζ₀ built on Ψ₀ and GR00T N1.7 achieves mean success rates of 63.6% and 79.5%, improving over the respective bases by 18.8 and 9.0 percentage points; on six real-world tasks, it reaches 78.3% and 85.0% success, with gains of 16.7 and 10.0 percentage points, and on GR00T it outperforms all compared seven-task joint policies.

topic_matches.title: MobileNeTTT: a Lightweight DNN-based Time-To-Transit Estimator for Visual Navigation
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes MobileNeTTT, a lightweight 1.95M-parameter neural network that estimates Time-to-Transit (TTT) for many visual features across the full field of view from a single monocular camera frame, aiming to provide a coarse depth proxy for bio-inspired robot navigation. MobileNeTTT is designed to be relatively insensitive to camera rotation and to automatically adapt TTT estimates to path geometry and obstacles, enabling simpler navigation control compared to large visual depth foundation models while remaining small enough for real-time execution on edge hardware. Simulation and laboratory robot experiments in dynamic and spatially complex environments validate that MobileNeTTT’s TTT-based navigation model can effectively guide mobile robots using monocular vision, with code, data, and video made available.
